claims.text: The base alloy has composition W38Ta36Cr15V11 in atomic percent.
The starting W38Ta36Cr15V11 material is nanocrystalline.
The starting alloy is produced by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
Unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits Cr and V segregation and a Cr/V-rich second phase under irradiation up to approximately 8 dpa.
The irradiation-associated Cr/V-rich precipitates in the unmodified alloy are approximately 3–5 nm in size.
The unmodified alloy exhibits only slight or negligible irradiation hardening.
No irradiation-induced dislocation loops are observed in the unmodified alloy after irradiation up to 8 dpa.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 0.5 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles during mechanical alloying before spark plasma sintering.
Processing will produce a uniform Y2O3 dispersion at grain boundaries and within grains.
Y2O3 nanoparticle interfaces will act as stable sinks for irradiation-induced point defects.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries and inhibit grain coarsening during high-temperature processing.
Absorption of point defects at the nanoparticle interfaces will enhance vacancy-interstitial recombination and lower surviving defect concentrations.
Lower point-defect concentrations will reduce Cr and V mobility and thereby inhibit their segregation and precipitation.
At approximately 8 dpa, Y2O3 addition will significantly reduce the volume fraction and size of irradiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitates relative to the unmodified alloy.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will retain negligible irradiation hardening relative to its pre-irradiation state and the unmodified reference.
Y2O3 addition will improve densification and structural integrity during bulk consolidation.
The proposed comparison applies at approximately 8 dpa and 450–600°C.
The 450–600°C irradiation interval is representative of fusion-relevant service conditions.
Failure to obtain at least a 30% reduction in precipitate volume fraction or size, or observation of increased irradiation hardening or degraded mechanical performance, would falsify the hypothesis.
